what: Which tools each laserbrain transport must expose. The stdio server and the hosted Worker are separate implementations with separate hand-maintained tool lists, and nothing compared them: local had 32, hosted had 15, and the gap was found by counting rather than by any check.

universal.what: Must exist on BOTH the stdio server and the hosted Worker. A divergence here is a bug.

local_only.what: Not yet on the hosted transport. Each is bridged to Python by the stdio server rather than implemented in it, so answering needs a subprocess the Worker cannot spawn. That is a fact about that server, not about the tool: laserscore moved to universal on 2026-08-30 by porting it, and the rest can follow. The note against each says what it would take, not why it is impossible.

tools.attention: reads the calibration table from disk
tools.capabilities: reads the working tree to report what is installed
tools.link_read: the link log is a local file
tools.link_whoami: the link log is a local file
tools.link_write: the link log is a local file
tools.mark_verdict: writes to the local verdict ledger
tools.similarity: loads a sentence-transformer model; a Worker has no Python runtime
